intake.domain: composition-only materials property prediction on small experimental tabular benchmarks (Matbench v0.1 composition tasks); ensemble combination and post-hoc residual correction of property predictors
data: official Matbench v0.1 5-fold splits only; every hyperparameter / expert / correction choice made by nested CV inside training folds; no test-fold use
intake.compute: one Windows workstation, 24 CPU cores, no GPU (CPU-only is a hard user constraint); no cloud GPU budget assumed
intake.expertise: applied ML / cheminformatics; author of SIG-Net (JCIM submission 2026-10-18, chemistry domain, not yet indexed) whose local out-of-fold residual correction was confirmed in a pre-registered replication (p = 0.016)
intake.baseline: Official Matbench v0.1 leaderboard per-task leaders (host-verified 2026-10-18): steels TPOT-Mat 79.95 MAE (MODNet v0.1.12 87.76); expt_gap Darwin 0.2865 MAE; expt_is_metal Darwin 0.9598; glass MODNet v0.1.12 0.9603. Literature comparators: MODNet@MM+MatterVial (dblp:journals/corr/abs-2509-03547), TabPFN-based ICL on Magpie features (semanticscholar:bcdf813b811e5323f5d3c6f53ff614c518303c98). Host note: leaderboard classification 'rocauc' equals balanced accuracy for most entries, indicating hard-label submissions.
intake.user_direction: Transfer cross-fitted stacking of diverse experts followed by a novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction (confirmed in my earlier SIG-Net paper) to composition-based materials property prediction on the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks (steels, expt_gap, expt_is_metal, glass)
intake.excluded_direction: CPU-only, official Matbench folds, honest nested cross-validation for every choice, no test-fold use
intake.limitation: Leading composition models are single global predictors or globally weighted combinations whose out-of-fold errors may carry composition-local structure; whether such structure can be recovered honestly (nested CV, tiny n, random folds on redundant data, hard-label classification scoring) is untested on these tasks. The user's prior confirmation of the local residual correction is in a different (chemistry) domain and is not part of the indexed literature.

bottleneck_statement: On the small Matbench composition tasks every current leader is one global descriptor-to-property map or one globally weighted combination: a feature-fused MODNet (dblp:journals/corr/abs-2509-03547), a single TabPFN in-context predictor on Magpie features (semanticscholar:bcdf813b811e5323f5d3c6f53ff614c518303c98), or a stack whose meta-learner applies one weight vector to every composition (doi:10.1038/s41467-024-55525-y), all scored on random 5-fold splits of chemically clustered, redundant datasets (arxiv:2005.00707). The structural property is this: when a global learner is fit to a small, clustered dataset, its out-of-fold errors are not exchangeable. They co-vary within chemical neighbourhoods (shared host element, shared chemical system, near-duplicate stoichiometries), and the ranking of experts can itself change between neighbourhoods. A loss averaged over the whole training fold cannot represent that structure, and nothing in these pipelines consumes it. Recovering it after the fact fails in two coupled ways that the retrieved work leaves open. (i) The recoverable signal exists only where a test composition has close training analogues. Under random folds that is a split-dependent quantity, so a locally borrowed gain may measure interpolation between near-duplicates rather than generalization. openalex:W4405590652 documents the in-distribution versus out-of-distribution gap for composition models, and semanticscholar:398586587c1f70079b3b60825e93ff651a519ff9 finds that a learned residual correction is needed most exactly where the reference data covers the target region least. (ii) At n = 312 (steels), the gain of any added post-hoc stage is about the size of fold-to-fold variation: MatterVial's steels improvement is 87.76 to 85.12 MAE, and it could not reproduce the reported glass 0.960 AUROC. So choosing that stage's configuration, even inside the training folds, can produce an apparent gain unless the variance of the selection is itself accounted for. On the two classification tasks the scored quantity compounds the problem. Most leaderboard 'rocauc' entries equal balanced accuracy, i.e. they are hard-label submissions (host-verified), while dblp:journals/corr/abs-2509-03547 reports a probability AUROC of 0.976 on expt_is_metal against a board leader of 0.9598. Ranking improvements from any combination stage are therefore not commensurable with the board. The anchor setting is the primary instance of this property; the broader class is any small, clustered tabular property benchmark scored on random splits with global learners.

closest_adjacent.summary_and_residue: Adds latent features from pretrained GNNs (ROOST, MEGNet, ORB), autoencoded MatMiner/OFM features and SISSO formulas to MatMiner inputs, and trains one MODNet per task on the official Matbench folds. Reported results: steels 85.12 MAE, expt_gap 0.290, expt_is_metal 0.976 AUROC; glass is not improved, and the authors could not replicate the 0.960 glass AUROC. Its residue: the combination happens at the feature level inside a single global model, so out-of-fold errors that remain locally structured are never modelled. Its expt_is_metal AUROC is probability-based, which is not commensurable with the hard-label leaderboard values. It also does not test whether the small steels gain (3%) exceeds fold or selection variance.

Uses the pretrained TabPFN v2.2.1 transformer as an in-context predictor on Magpie/MagpieEX composition features (and on ALIGNN/CGCNN embeddings for structure tasks), following the official Matbench splits, on an RTX 4090 GPU. Its residue: it is one global predictor per task, with no combination with other experts and no analysis of whether its out-of-fold errors are complementary to MODNet- or tree-type experts or concentrated in chemical neighbourhoods. Its inference cost and accuracy under the user's CPU-only constraint are not reported.

Stacks an electron-configuration model with two composition models grounded in different domain knowledge (stacked generalization) to predict thermodynamic stability, and reports better sample efficiency. Its residue: the level-1 learner combines experts with one global rule that does not vary with location in composition space; it is evaluated on stability, not on the small experimental Matbench tasks; and it has no stage acting on the stack's own out-of-fold residuals. [residue is abstract-level: fulltext fetch failed]

Fits a species-aggregated additive-kernel GPR on CHGNet's own 64-d atomic embeddings to learn and correct CHGNet's residual errors (a Δ-model), and uses the GP uncertainty inside an active-learning global structure search. Its residue: the correction's need is traced to missing local environments in the training data (Ag-S, Au-S), i.e. correction matters most where reference support is thinnest, yet the correction gets new DFT labels by active acquisition. A fixed offline benchmark has no such route, and the paper does not say how a residual correction should behave where there is no support. The setting is structure-based energies, not composition-only small tabular tasks.

Shows that physically informed atom encodings, compared with one-hot encodings, improve the out-of-distribution accuracy of composition (Roost/CrabNet-type) and structure models trained on small datasets, which documents that in-distribution benchmark accuracy overstates performance on novel chemistries. Its residue: it changes only the input representation of one global model. It neither quantifies how much of the reported random-split accuracy comes from test compositions having close training neighbours, nor studies ensembles or post-hoc corrections under that lens.

Defines the Matbench test suite: fixed random 5-fold splits, nested CV for the Automatminer reference, and MAE / ROC-AUC metrics. Its residue: random K-fold on datasets with heavy compositional redundancy leaves how close test compositions are to training compositions uncontrolled, and the classification protocol accepts submissions whose 'rocauc' collapses to balanced accuracy (hard labels), so entries are not scored on one common quantity.

Addresses two stacking pathologies, meta-learner ill-conditioning from prediction-space multicollinearity and calibration collapse, using a CKA redundancy filter, a small per-sample meta-feature gate and a spectrum-adaptive ridge penalty, all on large pools of vision backbones. Its residue: the per-sample gate is learned with abundant data. Whether any input-dependent combination can be estimated without overfitting at n of a few hundred to a few thousand, with nested selection, is untested.

Assigns each instance its most suitable base classifier through a meta-model (dynamic selection), and reports better accuracy and run time than bagging, boosting and stacking. Its residue: the per-instance choice is a hard selection judged on generic benchmarks. Its variance at very small n, its behaviour on instances far from any training competence region, and its use for regression residuals are not examined. [residue is abstract-level: not in fulltext pool]

what_phase_0_did_not_address: (additive; leaf sites L_mattervial, L_iclfm, L_ecsg) No retrieved leaf on these tasks establishes whether the out-of-fold errors of the leading global composition predictors (feature-fused MODNet, TabPFN in-context prediction) or of a globally weighted stack are exchangeable across composition space or concentrated in identifiable chemical neighbourhoods, nor whether the experts' relative accuracy reverses between neighbourhoods. The amount of residual signal that any post-hoc stage could recover on steels, expt_gap, expt_is_metal and glass is therefore unknown. — stakes: a practitioner building a multi-expert pipeline cannot tell beforehand whether a second stage can help at all on a given task, so CPU-weeks are spent on stages whose ceiling may be zero. Intellectually, the field's choice of a single global model as the reporting unit rests on an untested premise about where error lives.

(additive; leaf sites L_deltamodel, L_restgp, L_concrete_residual) No residual-correction leaf provides a correction whose expected effect is non-negative where local reference evidence is thin. The Δ-model leaf finds corrections are needed most exactly where training coverage is sparsest, but it relies on acquiring new labels there. The residual-GP and physics-residual leaves say nothing about what their correction does to a query with no close training analogue. A fixed offline benchmark offers no label acquisition, so the question is open in exactly the regime where it matters. — stakes: on steels (n = 312) a handful of atypical alloys dominate MAE, so a correction that extrapolates wrongly there erases or reverses the average gain. In discovery use, the novel compositions are the ones whose predictions are acted on, so a correction that is harmful off-support costs real experiments.

(additive; leaf sites L_mattervial, L_ecsg, L_leakfree_stack) No leaf on the small composition tasks reports whether its selected configuration's gain exceeds the variance introduced by selecting that configuration on the same few folds. MatterVial's steels improvement (87.76 to 85.12 MAE) and its unreplicated glass 0.960 both sit in a range where fold-to-fold noise plus choosing among many feature-group/stack variants can produce the difference. Leakage-free out-of-fold construction removes one bias but not this selection variance. — stakes: leaderboard 'wins' on steels and glass may be winner's-curse artefacts that a reviewer at Computational Materials Science cannot tell apart from real improvements. Any paper, including the user's, that claims a per-task SOTA from a few-percent gain at n = 312 risks a non-replicating headline, which conflicts directly with an honest-results commitment.

(additive; leaf site L_mattervial, inherited from the Matbench classification protocol) No leaf makes the classification scores on expt_is_metal and glass commensurable. Leaderboard 'rocauc' equals balanced accuracy for most entries (hard-label submissions), while MatterVial reports a probability AUROC of 0.976 against a board leader of 0.9598. It is therefore unknown which reported gains reflect better ranking and which reflect thresholding, and a combination stage that improves probability ranking can look either invisible or inflated depending on the submission format. — stakes: cross-entry SOTA comparisons on the two classification tasks are currently invalid as stated, and a CMS paper that compares a probability AUROC with the board's hard-label numbers would overclaim by about 0.02 AUROC from the metric alone. That is the kind of error a reviewer who knows the leaderboard will catch.

(subtractive; shared ancestor n_matbench_protocol: every leaf is evaluated under random 5-fold splits of redundant composition data) No retrieved paper tests whether improvements measured under the official random 5-fold splits depend on test compositions having near-neighbour or near-duplicate training compositions, that is, whether the random-split protocol is a valid estimator of the generalization that the improvement claims. — stakes: intellectually, published Matbench composition rankings, and especially any gain that borrows strength from nearby training points, may not transfer to novel chemistries (the physical-encoding leaf shows the in-distribution/out-of-distribution gap is real for these model families). Practically, a screening user who trusts a locally obtained leaderboard gain would carry it into exactly the out-of-support regime where it is least likely to hold.

(subtractive; shared ancestor n_global_erm / n_stacking: every leaf fits one global predictor or one globally fixed combination rule per task) Every retrieved leaf on composition tasks assumes that one fit per task, with the same parameters or weights for every composition, is the right predictive unit. This covers feature fusion into one MODNet, a single TabPFN context, and a meta-learner with one weight vector (ECSG, the leakage-free stack), as well as CORE-STACK+, whose per-sample gate is only demonstrated on large vision pools. No retrieved paper tests whether this homogeneity assumption is necessary for small, chemically clustered composition datasets rather than simply assumed. — stakes: intellectually, if the assumption fails, the leaderboard compares architectures on a quantity (one global fit) that hides where each method is actually reliable, and conclusions such as 'feature-based beats GNN on small sets' could be artefacts of averaging over heterogeneous neighbourhoods. Practically, users pick one 'best' model per property and inherit its worst-neighbourhood errors.

method_lineage.line: combining and post-hoc correcting global property predictors on small composition-descriptor benchmarks under cross-validated evaluation

nodes.method: Single global supervised predictor with K-fold cross-validation as the generalization estimate (Stone 1974; Geisser 1975)
nodes.move: root: fit one input-to-target map on all training data; estimate generalization by held-out folds
nodes.residual_problem: one map for the whole input space; random folds assume exchangeable samples; model choice made on the same folds biases the estimate

nodes.method: Stacked generalization (Wolpert 1992)
nodes.move: train a level-1 learner on out-of-fold (cross-validated) predictions of several level-0 learners instead of choosing one
nodes.residual_problem: how to constrain the level-1 learner; the combination rule is the same everywhere in input space

nodes.method: Stacked regressions with non-negative weights (Breiman 1996); Super Learner / cross-fitted convex combination (van der Laan, Polley, Hubbard 2007)
nodes.move: constrain level-1 weights (non-negative / convex) and give an oracle inequality for V-fold cross-fitted combination
nodes.residual_problem: oracle guarantee is asymptotic: says nothing about selection variance at n of a few hundred; one global weight vector

nodes.method: Residual regression on input space: regression-kriging of model residuals (geostatistics, 1990s); Δ-learning of a baseline model's error (Ramakrishnan et al. 2015)
nodes.move: fit a second model to the residual of a baseline as a function of the inputs (not only of the baseline prediction), borrowing strength from nearby training points
nodes.residual_problem: correction is applied regardless of how much local reference evidence exists; its bandwidth/strength must itself be selected

nodes.method: Nested cross-validation and model-selection bias (Varma & Simon 2006; Cawley & Talbot 2010)
nodes.move: separate the selection loop from the assessment loop so the reported score is not optimistically biased by tuning
nodes.residual_problem: removes bias in expectation but leaves high variance of the selected configuration at small n; does not by itself say whether a selected gain exceeds that variance

nodes.method: Magpie composition descriptors + random forest (Ward et al. 2016)
nodes.move: general-purpose fixed-length elemental-statistics descriptor for any composition, fed to one global tree ensemble
nodes.residual_problem: single global model; descriptor is permutation-averaged so near-identical stoichiometries map to near-identical features (redundancy)

nodes.method: Matbench v0.1 test suite + Automatminer reference (Dunn et al. 2020)
nodes.move: standardized tasks, fixed random 5-fold splits and nested-CV reference pipeline for comparing materials ML
nodes.residual_problem: random K-fold on compositionally redundant data leaves test-to-train proximity uncontrolled; classification entries scored inconsistently (hard-label 'rocauc' = balanced accuracy)

nodes.method: MODNet: feature selection + joint learning (De Breuck et al. 2020/2021)
nodes.move: relevance-redundancy feature selection on MatMiner features and joint multi-property NN to curb overfitting on small sets
nodes.residual_problem: one global network per task; locally structured residuals in composition space not modelled

nodes.method: Roost: stoichiometry-graph message passing (Goodall & Lee 2020)
nodes.move: learn composition representation end-to-end from weighted element graph instead of fixed descriptors
nodes.residual_problem: data-hungry on the smallest tasks; single global model

nodes.method: CrabNet: compositionally restricted attention (Wang et al. 2021)
nodes.move: transformer self-attention over element tokens with fractional-amount encoding
nodes.residual_problem: data-hungry on small sets such as steels; single global model

nodes.method: MODNet v0.1.12 leaderboard update (ensembled/tuned MODNet, ~2022-2023)
nodes.move: hyperparameter-optimized and ensembled MODNet submission; current glass leader 0.9603 and steels 87.76
nodes.residual_problem: averages multiple MODNets globally; glass score not reproduced by the anchor (dblp:journals/corr/abs-2509-03547)

nodes.method: AutoML pipeline search (TPOT, Olson et al. 2016) as applied in the 'TPOT-Mat' steels leaderboard entry
nodes.move: genetic search over scikit-learn pipelines per task; current steels leader 79.95 MAE
nodes.residual_problem: large pipeline search on n=312 is exactly the regime where selection variance can manufacture a gain; details of the entry's nesting not verified here

nodes.method: Darwin: fine-tuned LLM for materials property prediction (Xie et al. 2023)
nodes.move: text-based composition-to-property prediction with a domain-fine-tuned LLM; current expt_gap and expt_is_metal leader
nodes.residual_problem: GPU-heavy single global model; likely hard-label classification submission (rocauc = balanced accuracy)

nodes.method: TabPFN v1 prior-fitted network (Hollmann et al. 2022/2023)
nodes.move: amortized Bayesian prediction on small tabular data via a transformer pretrained on synthetic tasks
nodes.residual_problem: small-n/feature limits; one global in-context predictor; no domain-local structure

nodes.method: TabPFN v2 (Hollmann et al. 2025)
nodes.move: scaled prior-fitted tabular foundation model outperforming tuned trees on small data
nodes.residual_problem: generic tabular prior; does not exploit composition-local error structure; complementarity with domain experts unmeasured on Matbench

nodes.method: ICL foundation models (TabPFN + Magpie/MagpieEX) for materials property prediction
nodes.move: apply TabPFN in-context learning to composition and GNN-embedding features on official Matbench splits
nodes.residual_problem: single global predictor; no combination with other experts; OOF error structure and CPU cost not analysed

nodes.method: MODNet@MatMiner+MatterVial latent/SISSO features
nodes.move: fuse latent features of pretrained GNNs/MLIPs and symbolic-regression descriptors into MODNet inputs
nodes.residual_problem: feature-level fusion into one global model; glass not improved and 0.960 not reproduced; probability AUROC not commensurable with hard-label board; steels gain (3%) not tested against selection/fold variance

nodes.method: Cross-modal knowledge transfer for composition models
nodes.move: pretrain chemical language models on multimodal embeddings or generate structures to feed structure-aware predictors
nodes.residual_problem: gains on large tasks; smallest experimental tasks (steels, expt_gap) not shown to benefit; single global predictor

nodes.method: Physical atom encodings for OOD composition/structure models
nodes.move: replace one-hot atom encodings with physical-property encodings; evaluate on OOD splits
nodes.residual_problem: shows in-distribution accuracy overstates novel-chemistry accuracy but does not quantify how much random-split benchmark gains depend on near-neighbour test compositions; no ensembles/corrections

nodes.method: ECSG: electron-configuration model stacked with two domain-knowledge composition models
nodes.move: stacked generalization of composition experts with different inductive biases for stability prediction
nodes.residual_problem: global combination rule; no stage acting on the stack's OOF residuals; not evaluated on small experimental Matbench tasks (abstract-level)

nodes.method: LFS-FRAME leakage-free stacking (KAN + XGBoost)
nodes.move: strict out-of-fold meta-feature construction for heterogeneous base learners in multiclass classification
nodes.residual_problem: removes meta-feature leakage but not selection variance; global meta-learner; no residual stage; not materials

nodes.method: CORE-STACK+
nodes.move: precondition the meta-learner (CKA redundancy filter, per-sample gate, spectrum-adaptive ridge) against multicollinearity and calibration collapse
nodes.residual_problem: input-dependent combination demonstrated only with large vision pools; estimability at n of hundreds under nested selection untested

nodes.method: Dynamic Selection Best Model (DSBM)
nodes.move: meta-learned per-instance assignment of the best base classifier
nodes.residual_problem: hard per-instance selection; variance at tiny n and behaviour far from any competence region unexamined; classification only

nodes.method: ΔGP-CHGNet: GPR Δ-model on a foundation model's own embeddings
nodes.move: learn the residual of a universal potential with a species-aggregated additive-kernel GP on its internal atomic representations
nodes.residual_problem: correction is most needed where reference coverage is thinnest, and is fed there by active DFT acquisition; behaviour of the correction off-support without acquisition is unaddressed

nodes.method: Residual Tree Gaussian Process (ResTGP)
nodes.move: multi-resolution GP decomposition into predictive and residual processes along a dyadic tree
nodes.residual_problem: built for large spatial data; small-n, high-dimensional composition-feature residuals and off-support behaviour untested

nodes.method: Physics-informed hybrid ML with residual correction (concrete carbonation)
nodes.move: ML learns residual of a coarse physics model; variogram analysis of response surfaces
nodes.residual_problem: residual correction applied uniformly, not conditioned on local evidence; civil-engineering domain (abstract-level)

nodes.method: Review of benchmarking practices in materials AI
nodes.move: catalogues what Matbench/JARVIS measure (aggregate MAE/AUC on fixed splits) vs miss (distribution shift, uncertainty, reproducibility)
nodes.residual_problem: narrative review; does not quantify the split-proximity or hard-label scoring effects on actual Matbench composition rankings

nodes.method: Mixture of experts with input-dependent gating (Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan, Hinton 1991)
nodes.move: learn a gate that weights experts as a function of the input
nodes.residual_problem: same residual (global weights miss local expert reliability) via a jointly trained gate; gate overfits at small n

nodes.method: Dynamic classifier/ensemble selection by local competence (Woods, Kegelmeyer, Bowyer 1997; KNORA, Ko, Sabourin, Britto 2008)
nodes.move: for each query, select or weight experts by their accuracy on its k nearest training (validation) neighbours
nodes.residual_problem: local expert reliability via neighbourhood competence; unreliable when the neighbourhood is empty or noisy

nodes.method: Locally weighted regression / kNN smoothing of residuals (Cleveland 1979; Nadaraya-Watson 1964)
nodes.move: estimate a local correction as a kernel- or neighbour-weighted average of nearby residuals
nodes.residual_problem: locally structured residual via nonparametric smoothing; bandwidth selection and boundary/sparse-region variance

nodes.method: Shrinkage / partial pooling of local estimates toward a global estimate (James-Stein 1961; empirical Bayes; hierarchical models)
nodes.move: pull noisy local estimates toward the pooled value in proportion to their local information
nodes.residual_problem: the 'thin local evidence' problem via variance-weighted shrinkage

nodes.method: Applicability domain / distance-to-model reliability (QSAR: Tropsha, Gramatica, Gombar 2003; Sheridan et al. 2004)
nodes.move: flag or down-weight predictions for queries far from the training set in descriptor space
nodes.residual_problem: off-support reliability via distance thresholds; does not itself improve accuracy

nodes.method: Leave-cluster-out / blocked cross-validation (Meredig et al. 2018 LOCO-CV; Roberts et al. 2017 blocked CV)
nodes.move: hold out whole clusters of similar samples so test points lack near-duplicate training neighbours
nodes.residual_problem: random-split optimism under redundancy, via split redesign (not usable as the official score, but as a diagnostic)

nodes.method: Fold-variance-aware comparison of learners (Dietterich 1998 5x2cv; Nadeau & Bengio 2003 corrected resampled t-test)
nodes.move: account for overlap between CV training sets when testing whether one learner beats another
nodes.residual_problem: whether a CV gain is real, via variance-corrected tests; does not by itself include the variance of the selection step

nodes.method: Probability calibration of classifiers and ensembles (Platt 1999; Zadrozny & Elkan 2002)
nodes.move: map scores to calibrated probabilities before combination/thresholding
nodes.residual_problem: probability-vs-label quality on classification; does not resolve a benchmark that scores hard labels as 'rocauc'

method_lineage.notes: (1) PROVENANCE DISCIPLINE: nodes marked retrieved:<paper_id> are grounded and citable. Parametric nodes (Wolpert, Breiman/Super Learner, regression-kriging/Δ-learning, nested CV, Roost, MODNet v0.1.12, TPOT-Mat, Darwin, TabPFN v1 and all collateral nodes) are awareness-only, with approximate dates and attributions. They are not prior-art citations. The user's own SIG-Net (JCIM submission, unindexed, chemistry domain) is not in lit_table and appears here only as intake context, never as a node. (2) ANTI-FABRICATION: the 2-4y band (MODNet v0.1.12, TPOT-Mat, Darwin, TabPFN v1) is the lowest-confidence band. TPOT-Mat's protocol in particular is unverified beyond the host's leaderboard check. (3) REGRESSION MAP (job b), named concretely: the components of the user's stated direction each land on an existing node. 'Cross-fitted stacking of diverse experts' = n_superlearner (Breiman 1996 / Super Learner 2007, convex V-fold cross-fitted combination). A 'local out-of-fold residual correction' = n_residual_on_input (regression-kriging, Δ-learning) and C_local_smoothing (kNN/kernel residual smoothing). 'Novelty damping' = C_shrinkage (partial pooling toward the global prediction) and C_applicability_domain (distance-to-training down-weighting). Input-dependent expert weighting, if proposed, = C_moe / C_des. A candidate whose novelty claim rests on any of these mechanisms alone is a regression and will be judged as engineering at CMS. Defensible novelty must come from what is shown about the failure at the frontier-leaf residuals (where composition-space error lives, off-support behaviour, selection variance at n = 312, split-proximity dependence, classification-score commensurability), not from the component mechanisms. (4) COLLATERAL NODES are sidelines attached by shared residual_problem. They are never gap sites and never the shared ancestor for the subtractive gaps; those are read from n_matbench_protocol (all leaves evaluated on its random folds) and n_global_erm / n_stacking (all leaves fit one global map or one global combination rule). (5) Shallow-band caveat: the composition-ML chain is young (Magpie 2016 onward), so the deep bands come from the general ML/statistics ancestry, which is where the regression risk for this direction actually lies.

domain_pattern_distribution.notes: The most-used pattern is structural_prior_encoding (better descriptors or encodings for one model). The closest_adjacent papers that use it or unify_into_shared_representation share one stopping point: they improve a single global predictor's input and stop there, without examining where its out-of-fold error lives or how the benchmark split and score shape the reported gain. On-topic set (23): the 42 tagged rows minus 19 flagged off-core in their gap text (needs structure/XRD/charge density, interatomic potentials, design-side, extraction, unrelated 'stacked' sense, off-domain optimisation/spectroscopy); the 39 outside_taxonomy rows, including the duplicate LLM4Mat-bench and XStacking records, are excluded by rule.
